design.blocks: 8x8 contiguous, 3 px guard, roles assigned before any score is computed
design.split: one seeded 50/50 split into a selection half and a calibration half; the spacing is chosen on the selection half and certified on the calibration half
design.conformal_method: max-over-settings one-sided split conformal (Lei et al. JASA 2018 Algorithm 2 / Theorem 2.2)
design.unit: one spatial block's DTI against the off-catalogue lidar scarp-peak instrument
design.controls: the random control uses the same greedy spaced selection, spacing and per-block budget as the candidate (mass-matched); the h33 reference and H47-C1 controls are used at their own emission, restricted to the block

conformal.target: one future exchangeable public-catalogue block score vector
limitations: Marginal prediction coverage for one block, not all future blocks or a pooled nonlinear DTI.
Spatial separation does not establish geological exchangeability.
Public catalogue labels differ from expert-private new-fault labels.
Adaptive leaderboard submissions are not exchangeable calibration units.
Instrument L is derived from a lidar product that shares a physical quantity (slope) with the field's input band; it is an optimistic instrument for this field.
Spatial separation does not establish geological exchangeability; the conformal floor is conditional on that assumption and is not a private-label guarantee.
The screen does not spend a competition submission slot and reads no private label.
Owner-reported scores and the d2.8 reference raster are not organiser receipts.
